card vi-levels  [proto]
The agent places each card in the tree; the person corrects by request
why: The agent's placement is usually right. A correction costs one request, so placing by hand would be work for no gain.

The agent decides the level of every card it writes: the parent, and whether to promote or demote it with werk move. It does not ask first.

The person refines the tree afterwards. They ask for a reposition in chat, and the agent runs the move.

One rule for the agent: do not build a chain of single-child cards. A parent with one child is a sign that the two are one decision. Merge the child into the parent, or put it beside the parent, unless it is a separate decision that will get siblings soon.

Measured on the map: 42 of 110 parents have exactly one child card. Four of those start a chain of three or more, for example #ro-unchal, #ro-live and #ro-optparent.

unchallenged counts who:you cards only
why: Counting every decided card put the number at 44 of 49. A count that sits near its maximum ranks nothing.
subtree: 3 cards, 3 decided

49 decided cards. 5 have an option recorded against them: #tracker, #st-merge, #pr-now, #werk-onechat, #werk-approve. 12 option nodes in the whole log.

The split by who decides is the finding:

| who | decided | with options |
| --- | --- | --- |
| you | 19 | 4 |
| me | 28 | 0 |
| prototype | 1 | 1 |

A who:me card is a reversible call the agent made and reported. An option on it is noise. So the population #al-two cares about is who:you, and there the number is 15 of 19 with no contrast, not 44 of 49.

card ro-live  [decided]
Record a rejected option the moment it's weighed, not after
why: unchallenged cannot tell "no option was weighed" from "an option was weighed and never written down." Both #ro-unchal and #vi-backend were corrected after the fact for exactly this.
subtree: 2 cards, 2 decided

Same discipline CLAUDE.md already states for depends_on: record it the moment you create a card, or it cannot be reconstructed later. Extended here to alternative_to.

The rule: when a decision comes from real contrast in conversation — a named alternative, a reason it was rejected — add that alternative as its own option node with --why_not, and link it alternative_to the decided card, in the same turn.

node src/cli.ts add <id>:opt0 --kind option --title "..." --why_not "..."
node src/cli.ts link <id>:opt0 <id> --type alternative_to

Skipping this made two cards indistinguishable from a decision made with no contrast at all, until someone noticed and asked. #ro-unchal:opt0 (count every decided card, rejected as too much noise) and #vi-backend:opt0 (tracker owns state, rejected for losing ordered event history) were both added after the fact, not at decision time.

This is now in CLAUDE.md, in the same section as the depends_on rule, and in the agent's persistent memory for this project, so it survives a session boundary.

  -> refines         ro-unchal  unchallenged counts who:you cards only
  -> supported_by    ro-unchal  unchallenged counts who:you cards only
  -> supported_by    vi-backend  The tracker is a publish target. log.jsonl stays the spine
  -> supported_by    ro-unchal:opt0  Count every decided card, regardless of who
  -> supported_by    vi-backend:opt0  The tracker owns state; werk reads and writes through it
  <- alternative_to  ro-live:opt0  Backfill the option only when the marker flags it
  <- refines         ro-optparent  An option needs alternative_to only, not refines

An option needs alternative_to only, not refines
why: Using --parent on an option node also adds a refines edge. The card then renders twice on its parent's page: once under 'N below', once under 'Options'. #ro-live's own command pattern already omits --parent — this is a mistake in how I called it, not a gap in the rule.

The correct call, exactly as #ro-live already states it:
node src/cli.ts add <id>:opt0 --kind option --title "..." --why_not "

All four chains have one cause. A card uses `refines` to point at the card that *triggered* it, not at the card it is *a part of*. Each child also carries `depends_on` to the same card, so the `refines` edge holds no extra information.

| Chain | What each link is | Flatten to |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `#ro-unchal` → `#ro-live` → `#ro-optparent` | A measurement → a rule that came from it → a fix to how the rule is called | Merge `#ro-optparent` into `#ro-live` (it is one line: "no `--parent`"). Move `#ro-live` up under `#rollup`, with `depends_on #ro-unchal`. |
| `#vi-sysdiag-grid-lanewall` → `junction` → `hop` | An incident ("Resolved: …") → the mechanism → how it renders | Merge `lanewall` into `junction` as its why. `junction` goes under `#vi-sysdiag-grid-gaps`. `hop` stays below `junction`, because it has its own two options. |
| `#st-tier-say` → `#st-tier-event` → `#st-run-issue` | Three steps, each one caused by the step before | Move all three up as siblings under `#st-tier-who`, next to `#st-tier-default`. The `depends_on` edges keep the order. |
| `#lp-two` → `#lp-checks` → `#lp-checks-scripts` | Two layers, but only the check layer is below it | This chain is different. The judgement layer, `#lp-prod-judge`, sits under `#lp-rubric-prod`. Add `refines #lp-two` to it, so `#lp-two` gets its second child. `#lp-checks-scripts` stays below `#lp-checks`. |

After these changes, no chain has three or more cards. The result is two merges and four moves.

The rule in `#vi-levels` needs one more test: "Does the child answer a part of the parent's question, or did the parent only cause it? If it only caused it, put the child beside the parent and add `depends_on`."
